title: NIST: standard atomic weight of Zinc (Zn, Z=30) is 65.38(2)
summary: NIST prints the standard atomic weight field of Zinc (Zn, Z=30) as 65.38(2), with the isotope rows in the same file.
body: PubChem's periodic-table row names atomic number 30, symbol Zn, as Zinc. The NIST compositions file prints the standard atomic weight of Zinc as 65.38(2). The parenthesis is the uncertainty NIST prints on the last digits of that standard atomic weight. It is an evaluated standard, not one laboratory weighing of one sample. Range in isotopic composition of normal terrestrial material prevents a more precise standard atomic weight being given; the tabulated atomic-weight value and uncertainty should be applicable to normal materials. Isotope rows in the same file: Zn-64 relative atomic mass 63.92914201(71), isotopic composition 0.4917(75); Zn-66 relative atomic mass 65.92603381(94), isotopic composition 0.2773(98); Zn-67 relative atomic mass 66.92712775(96), isotopic composition 0.0404(16); Zn-68 relative atomic mass 67.92484455(98), isotopic composition 0.1845(63); Zn-70 relative atomic mass 69.9253192(21), isotopic composition 0.0061(10). A relative atomic mass is scaled to carbon-12. An isotopic composition, when the field is not blank, is a representative mole fraction, not a new assay made for this card. The symbols for an interval, a parenthesis, a bracket, and a # mark are defined on world.chemistry.nist-atomic-weight-notation. This standard atomic weight is not the Chemistry WebBook molecular-weight field, which is a different catalog entry when one exists.
